newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa futures called flat to $5 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa futures called flat to $5 lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open unchanged to $5 per tonne lower Monday, in line with a weak performance in London overnight, traders said.

London cocoa futures were softer early Monday, pressured by commission house selling. Benchmark LIFFE March cocoa was down one stg a tonne at the midday break, at 963 stg, off the low of 956 stg. December was three stg weaker, at 934 stg.

New York cocoa futures ended a slightly weaker Friday, with benchmark December futures falling $2 on the day, to $1,360, its lowest settlement in three weeks, having traded from $1,357 to $1,371. Second-position March was down $1, to $1,389, while the outer months settled unchanged to down $7.
On the charts, December support was seen at $1,350, while a chart gap created last week at $1,378-1,382 offered solid resistance.

The latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report showed non-commercial long positions increased by 4,082 lots in the two weeks ended October 22, to 12,677 lots. Non-commercial short positions decreased by 6,291 lots to 838 lots.
Commercial long positions fell by 2,560 lots in the two weeks, to 50,450 lots and commercial short positions rose by 8,359 lots to 69,883 lots.
Nonreportable long positions rose 2,051 lots to 18,227 lots, while nonreportable short positions rose 1,505 lots to 10,683 lots in the two weeks.
On the fundamental side, the USDA said late Friday that world cocoa grindings would be 2.775 million tonnes in 1996/97, up from 2.697 the previous year.
Gross world production was estimated at 2.660 million tonnes in 1996/97, down from 2.876 million tonnes in 1995/96, the USDA said.
